headline: Director, Tax Credit and and Energy Advisory Services Group, KPMG Washing National Tax

location.linkedinText: Washington, District of Columbia, United States

about:
Susan Reaman is a Director in the newly formed Washington National Tax Credit and Energy Advisory Services Group where she specializes in advising companies on the low-income housing and the new markets tax credit transactional and compliance matters.

Prior to joining KPMG, Ms. Reaman was Counsel and Senior Tax Policy Advisor at Nixon Peabody LLP, Washington, DC where she advised clients on new markets, low-income housing, historic, and renewable energy tax credits transactions. She also helped with broader issues of tax credit compliance and compliance matters involving state housing agencies. 

Prior to joining Nixon Peabody, Mrs. Reaman had over a 30-year career with the IRS Office of Chief Counsel.  She was the former Chief Counsel Branch Chief with responsibility for low-income, new markets, rehabilitation, and energy tax credits. 

.

about: With over 30 years of experience in complex, cross border, tax, I am an accomplished leader with notable financial, business change, and people achievements in both national and global contexts. experience.description: I lead a talented team of international tax professionals serving large corporate and asset management clients with diverse cross-border tax needs. I serve both foreign and US multinationals, including KPMG’s largest publicly listed clients. His experience includes successful IPOs and pre-IPO spinoffs, leading tax consulting for a complex Chapter 11 case, converting global business structures to more efficient centralized models, consolidating legal entities for business flexibility, buy-side and sell-side due diligence, effective tax rate planning, and assisting clients with global tax law changes, including BEPS 2.0 and managing tax matters related to business-driven changes. publications.title: Taxation in China - A Look Back at 2012 Developments, With Change Comes Challenges
publications.description:
The year 2012 was one of change for tax policy in China. Throughout the year, KPMG LLP’s Taxation in China webcast series provided updates on a number of key tax developments to help multinationals understand the complex tax system in China and how current or planned operations may be affected. The impact of these developments will continue in 2013 and beyond.
  
In this one-hour webcast, professionals from KPMG International member firms in China and the United States take another look at several major 2012 tax developments through case studies, including:
 
  ■VAT reform – What unexpected implications have arisen for production and operations departments?
 ■Nonresident taxation – What practical problems have resulted from Announcement 30, which provided guidance on how to qualify as a "beneficial owner" under income tax treaties?
 ■Tax refunds for exports – How can companies comply with the new regulations under Notice 39 and Announcement 24 effectively and efficiently?
 ■Equity contributions – What are the implications of the regulations on capital contribution with equity involving foreign-invested enterprises for companies considering or undergoing restructuring?

publications.title: Market Entry into China
publications.description:
This webcast provides an overview of China's business environment and practices, as well as how companies have succeeded in the past.
 
Moderated by Mark Barnes, partner in charge of KPMG LLP's High Growth Markets, the presenters include Thomas Stanley, COO of KPMG's Global China Practice; David Frey, partner, Management Consulting, KPMG in China; David Ling, partner, KPMG in China; and Rodney Lawrence, national principal in charge of KPMG's U.S. International Corporate Services practice.
 
Following a discussion on China's FDI environment, the presenters focus on the modes of entry and key considerations of investing in China, practical set issues and requirements, as well as specific stories of success and cases of failures.

publications.title: Key Tax Developments in China
publications.description:
Two senior tax professionals from KPMG in China -Tax Partner Abe Zhao and Global Transfer Pricing Services Director Leonard Zhang - will provide an update on tax developments in China in the context of topics and types of issues they have been discussing with U.S. companies over the last several weeks, during a coast-to-coast tour of many U.S. cities. Zhao and Zhang will be joined on the webcast by KPMG LLP's Linda Zhang, partner in charge of the U.S. China practice, and Rod Lawrence, U.S. principal in charge of International Corporate Tax, for their insights on the following areas:
 ■China's tax restructuring rules
 ■Nonresident taxation - impact of Circular 601 and Circular 698
 ■Transfer pricing in China - updates, recent developments, and key trends

publications.description: NEW YORK, May 10, 2011/PRNewswire/ -- A majority of multinational company tax executives predict that a broadened international regulatory focus on increased transparency will be the most significant change their company can expect in international taxation over the next year, according to a survey by KPMG LLP, the U.S. audit, tax and advisory firm.  Copy of survey for 2011 and 2012 available by requet

publications.title: Extension to Exclude Certain CFC Loans from Deemed Dividend Treatment:
publications.description:
Earlier this year, the Internal Revenue Service issued a notice that extended for one more year an
elective exclusion of certain short-term Controlled Foreign Corporation (CFC) loans to U.S.
shareholders from deemed dividend treatment. This article provides a general discussion of
Section 956 and highlights key aspects of the notice and the underlying election. This article also
provides some “rules of thumb” in applying the notice.

publications.title: Treasury Keeps the Spotlight on Earnings Stripping
publications.description:
Congress continues to be concerned with income shifting on cross-border investment in the United States through intercompany debt. This article provides a refresher of the so-called “earnings stripping” rules of Section 163(j), highlights a new compliance requirement for 2008, and details
some potential concerns.

publications.title: Remembering FIRPTA’s Withholding in Today’s Economy
publications.description:
FIRPTA's withholding tax provisions are onerous and can arise in the least expected places. The withholding tax is 10% of consideration and thus can be a significant item to miss. There has been
recent guidance on a number of issues from the IRS recently and this article highlights certain requirements and traps to avoid.  To obtain a copy, email author

publications.title: The Current Liquidity Crisis: Gaining Use of Foreign Subsidiary’s Cash
publications.description: In today's financial climate companies are looking to reduce debt.  Oftentimes, multinationals find that their foreign subsidiaries are profitable and have surplus cash.  Treasurers would like to repatriate that to the US to pay down parent level debt.  However, there are numerous tax issues related to that plan that often put Treasurers off.

publications.title: Credit Crunch: Traps to Avoid When Agreeing to Additional Security
publications.description:
This article highlights a number of situations that the authors have seen cause a U.S. multinational
to have an unexpected corporate income tax expense. These, plus several noted opportunities,
reiterate the benefit that Treasurers obtain from working closely with their tax directors and advisers
during the debt negotiation process

publications.title: Planning for the Lapse of Section 954(c)(6)
publications.description:
Section 954(c)(6) lapses at the end of the year and, unless it is extended, this will represent an unwelcome return of subpart F for many multinationals. This article explores options multinationals have to maintain their current subpart F position and comments on various federal tax issues that
practitioners should keep in mind in analyzing options.

publications.title: Foreign Multinational Tax Filing Requirements
publications.description: This article reviews the requirements for a foreign multinational to file US federal income tax returns, even in the absence of a permanent establishment. It outlines the penalties that apply for not filing. Finally, it reviews a number of scenarios and provides possible approaches for the advisor and the foreign multinational to consider.

publications.title: Foreign Investors:Obtaining Reduced Rates of Tax Under Penalties of Perjury
publications.description:
This article outlines the documentation foreign investors must provide and will use examples of
investment structures commonly seen in practice. It does not attempt to highlight when particular
forms of entity are regarded as “resident” in a treaty jurisdiction for the purposes of claiming benefits—that is a whole topic to itself given the proliferation of limitation of benefits clauses in our
newer tax treaties.  For copy of article email author

publications.title: The ‘CFC Look-Through’ Rule: New Flexibility in International Tax Planning
publications.description: It is increasingly rare for tax directors of U.S. multinationals to get good news — so one of the provisions in the latest Tax Act2 (enacted in May 2006) may have felt like Christmas come early. The excitement was caused by the CFC (‘controlled foreign corporation’) look-through rule. This article explains the effect of this new provision and the benefits it may bring. We also consider a number of risk areas when estimating this year’s federal income tax liability and the effective tax rate in this year’s financial statements.

publications.title: The Partial Repeal of Subpart F in the Services Context: New Flexibility
publications.description:
The Treasury Department and IRS recently issued Notice 2007-13 (“the Notice”) which announces
that they will amend the substantial assistance regulations2 with general effect to tax years
beginning on or after January 1, 2007. The Notice updates the 1968 regulations for changes in business activities that have occurred over the last 40 years. More importantly, the changes may reduce the amount of income includible in U.S. federal taxable income pursuant to subpart F, which could reduce the amount of federal income tax payable and favorably impact the global effective tax rate. This article discusses the new rules and their potential benefits and highlights actions tax directors
should consider for the current year.

As a Managing Director, I have increased responsibilities from my director role, increasing my client relationship and client management responsibilities.  I am responsible for contracting and negotiation of scope/fees on all of my projects and ultimately am accountable for client delivery.  I am still a key point of contact for buy side / finance integration, accounting operations, and technical accounting in areas of business combinations, foreign currency, inventory, IFRS/GAAP, and consolidations.  As a Managing Director, some of complex projects I have led which I have responsibility for include:

- Led a team of KPMG professionals in the USA, as well as Austrian and Australian member firms through a transformative reorganization of a global entity.  The support involved working with technical accounting, general ledger, reporting, technology, tax, and treasury teams as they deconsolidate and reorganize dozens of legal entities, treating the project as dozens of separations and then dozens of integrations.

- Supported a large multinational company through a transformative ERP implementation which required establishment of numerous legal entity ledgers to support new consolidation procedures, as well a supporting with multiple legal entity rationalizations in parallel with the ERP implementation.

When I was Director in the Accounting Advisory Services practice in KPMG's Deal Advisory group, specialized in accounting, financial reporting, and operational integration for complex mergers, acquisitions, and other strategic initiatives.  During that time I was a contributing author to a firm publication on asset acquisitions.   As a Director, I was a frequent instructor at KPMG’s national training center in Orlando, having responsibility for creating and delivering content on the subjects of business combinations and foreign currency matters.

Some of my recent client projects I led a Director include:

- Led a 20+ person team in the US and UK that assisted a global consumer products company in executing a complex legal entity reorganization.   The majority of this project spanned a 2.5 year period covering hundreds of business units in over 50 countries.  I worked closely with client international tax, treasury, IT, and accounting teams all over the world.

- Led the accounting and project management efforts for 30+ member team for a first of its kind project where a publicly traded financial technology company acquired a privately held bank, resulting in an overhaul to the fintech’s operating and reporting model as they became a bank.  Cross functional support was provided across multiple workstreams such as general ledger accounting, SEC reporting, credit, internal audit, human resources, tax, technology, and regulatory matters.

- Supported a newly created platform company for a private equity sponsor as they acquired eight companies over a 12- month period.  My support consisted of establishing monthly reporting processes, which included consolidation framework and implementing a monthly closing calendar for all acquisitions, board reporting packages, technical accounting support, and support with external audits.

My incredible 17 year run at Skoda Minotti started as a subsidiary of a public company, then that leadership team of that subsidiary left that public company and started their own firm in 2001 with less than 40 employees in Northeast Ohio.  By the time I left in 2015, I become part of that leadership team that helped the firm grow to over 400 employees, with 2 locations in Ohio and 1 in Florida and become a six-time Inc. 500 award recipient.

During my proud 17 years at the firm, I worked in the areas of assurance/auditing and income taxes, allowing to be provide a unique perspective to supporting clients.  My client base ranged from entrepreneurial companies and start-ups to mature $250mm privately held companies.  I led some of the larger audits of the firm, advised my clients through their various acquisitions, and supported my clients through IRS examinations.  I also have experience in litigation matters.

I contributed to the organization of over 700 live events throughout the world, ranging mostly from concerts at local clubs / arenas / stadiums, but also supported in numerous multi-day US festivals in NYC, LA, Las Vegas, Chicago, and Austin.  I have also supported global touring acts with record setting crowds in Europe, Canada, and South America.  I also have experience with live and recorded televised award shows and galas commanding an executive presence.  My specialty is in event security, but often times, this turns into production support and event management.    I work closely with promoters, local staffing crews, local law enforcement and military to ensure and fun and safe event.

headline: Life Sciences & Healthcare Consultant
about:
Seasoned professional adept at merging business acumen skills with a technical background in Regulatory Affairs, Compliance and Quality in Life Sciences and Healthcare to drive companies in growth and profitability to the P&L.  

I have deep experience in full lifecycle product development from ideation (gathering the requirements, clinical operations, LEAN manufacturing, and go-to-market strategies) to launch using stage gate at pharmaceutical industry leaders such as Merck, Bayer, GlaxoSmithKline (GSK), and St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital.  I have led multiple cross-functional teams on product development projects simultaneously by working with marketing, clinical operations, engineering, R&D, manufacturing, pricing, and sales. 

I have led many global Regulatory and Quality digital transformation and system implementation projects with cross-functional teams from Regulatory, Quality, Medical Affairs, Operations, and IT to support the product development and commercialization of Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices.

Able to create global market strategies, evaluate firm financial health, audit brands, conduct market research, product positioning, thoroughly analyze business data using data mining tool and techniques, predictive analytics, and consumer insights to identify trends and make recommendations for domestic and foreign markets.

I hold an MBA in Business Data Analytics & Marketing, MS in Integrated Marketing Communications, and a BS in Chemistry as well as industry certifications. 

Regulatory Affairs Certification - RAC RAPS, Regulatory Affairs Professional Society
Certified Medical Device Auditor - CMDA ASQ, American Society of Quality
Certified Quality Auditor - CQA ASQ, American Society of Quality

My expertise is applying a consultative approach to change management and integrations of businesses due to turnarounds and acquisition as well as business process development utilizing Six Sigma. Well regarded collaborator and empathetic leader.

headline: Strategic Operations & Finance Leader | Enterprise Transformation | Program Execution | LSS Black Belt | Driving Scalable Cost Optimization & Organizational Efficiency
about:
I am a Strategic Operations and Finance Leader with a proven track record of driving enterprise-wide transformation, optimizing supply chains, and delivering cost-saving initiatives that enhance long-term organizational performance.

In my current role as Enterprise Strategic Affordability Manager for the F-35 program at Lockheed Martin, I lead initiatives that have resulted in a 7.5% labor allocation reduction across all business functions, millions in lifecycle cost savings, and significant improvements in parts availability and procurement speed. I regularly brief the Executive Leadership Team, turning complex data into actionable insights to inform strategic planning and resource allocation across a $4.5B project portfolio.

I have led cross-functional teams across engineering, finance, operations, and logistics to execute scalable solutions that reduce risk, improve decision-making, and drive mission readiness. From implementing sustainability-aligned supply chain models to launching a Digital Transformation Financial Academy with the NGA and CIA, I specialize in solving complex problems with clarity, precision, and measurable results.

Whether transforming cost structures in aerospace or advising C-level stakeholders on operational strategy, I bring a balance of financial acumen, technical insight, and team leadership to every challenge.

I hold an MBA and am certified as a Lean Six Sigma Black Belt—equipping me with the analytical rigor and process improvement discipline to lead high-stakes, cross-functional initiatives and deliver enterprise-level outcomes.

experience.description:
As a Senior Associate in KPMG’s Finance Transformation practice, I am leading the operational and financial transition of a biotechnology client’s R&D facility into a fully commercialized manufacturing operation. My work integrates strategic cost accounting, process design, and systems enablement to establish sustainable profitability and compliance within a rapidly scaling environment.

I collaborate cross-functionally across Finance, R&D, and Supply Chain to implement standard costing models, define SKU-level cost structures, and align product lifecycle costing with commercial readiness. Through this engagement, I’m enabling the client to move from innovation to commercialization with financial transparency, scalability, and strategic decision-making capability.

Led the design and implementation of a standard costing framework to support the client’s transition from R&D operations to commercial-scale production, enabling accurate product cost visibility and pricing strategy alignment.

Partnered with finance, manufacturing, and supply chain leadership to establish SKU-level cost structures, labor routings, and variance analysis processes within the ERP environment.

Developed and implemented scalable financial operating models that standardized cost tracking, improved gross margin accuracy, and established the foundation for commercial profitability reporting

As a Managing Partner for a construction and real estate business in Chicago, I played a pivotal role in overseeing both residential home developments and a commercial strip mall. My responsibilities spanned across leasing, financial management, and property maintenance, ensuring long-term tenant satisfaction and asset profitability.

Key responsibilities included:

Rent Collection & Lease Negotiation – Managed tenant payments, drafted lease agreements, and negotiated terms for both residential and commercial storefronts.

Market Analysis & Tenant Acquisition – Conducted research to determine competitive rental rates, sourced new tenants, and optimized occupancy.

Property Maintenance & Repairs – Coordinated with contractors and service providers to oversee repairs, renovations, and facility upkeep.

Financial & Budgeting Oversight – Assisted in developing budget forecasts, tracking property expenses, and ensuring timely payment of property taxes.

Commercial Real Estate Operations – Worked closely with small business owners, handling lease structuring, rent escalations, and business development strategies for commercial tenants.

This experience gave me a strong foundation in real estate investment, property operations, and financial planning, allowing me to develop a business-owner mindset while managing both residential and commercial properties efficiently.

Founded Bent Trail Woodworks to bring unique, handcrafted wood and metal creations to life, specializing in custom furniture, home decor, and specialty welding projects. With a passion for craftsmanship and innovation, I built a workshop that delivers high-quality, made-to-order pieces tailored to clients' visions.

Key Responsibilities & Achievements:

Custom Design & Fabrication – Created bespoke furniture, home goods, and decorative pieces with a focus on precision craftsmanship.

Metal & Wood Integration – Combined woodworking with welding techniques to produce one-of-a-kind hybrid designs.

Client Collaboration – Worked closely with customers to transform ideas into reality, ensuring satisfaction through tailored consultations.

Operations & Business Growth – Managed end-to-end production, from material sourcing to final assembly, ensuring efficiency and quality control.

Tool & Process Optimization – Leveraged industry techniques to maximize productivity and craftsmanship..

Passionate about blending traditional woodworking with modern welding techniques, ensuring every project reflects top-tier craftsmanship and creativity.

My work directly supports long-term sustainment and mission capability across one of the most advanced aircraft platforms in the world.

Key Achievements:

Directed labor hour forecasting and reporting across the entire F-35 enterprise, presenting data-driven insights to the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) to inform strategic resource allocation.

Served as Program Management Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, leading a program-wide labor reduction initiative that achieved a 7.5% reduction in total labor allocation across all business functions.

Developed and executed cost optimization strategies across procurement, maintenance, and logistics to improve operational affordability and long-term sustainment.

Managed and executed Lean projects to drive enterprise-wide process improvements, cost savings, and alignment with strategic goals.

Collaborated with suppliers and internal teams to identify and eliminate supply chain bottlenecks, accelerating parts delivery and improving readiness outcomes.

Contributed to improved parts availability, reduced procurement delays, and increased executive-level decision support through data transparency.

Designed customized supply chain models aligned with environmental sustainability goals, balancing cost efficiency with operational resilience.

Fostered cross-functional collaboration across engineering, finance, operations, and logistics to implement integrated, performance-driven solutions.

projects.title: Automated Arbitrage Trading Bot on MetaTrader
projects.description:
Project Summary:
Designed, built, and deployed a fully automated arbitrage trading algorithm on MetaTrader, leveraging latency differences across brokers to generate consistent profit with minimal manual intervention.

Key Achievements:
	•	Algorithm Development: Created a custom arbitrage trading algorithm capable of identifying and executing trades based on real-time price discrepancies between two brokers. Programmed logic for dynamic trade sizing, slippage control, and spread thresholds.

	•	Infrastructure Setup: Deployed the MetaTrader platform on a high-speed virtual private server (VPS) to ensure low latency and 24/7 uptime. Integrated broker APIs for data feeds and order execution.

	•	Capital Efficiency: Grew a $300 initial investment into over $5,000 in just 8 months through disciplined, automated micro-trades. Achieved this with strict risk management parameters and adaptive stop-loss configurations.

	•	Performance Monitoring: Implemented custom logging and analytics tools to track PnL, execution lag, win ratios, and latency variations. Regularly optimized the algorithm based on trade performance data.

	•	Scalability Proof-of-Concept: Validated the algorithm’s scalability by running parallel simulations across different currency pairs and timeframes, preparing the system for larger capital deployment.

Outcome:
Successfully demonstrated the viability of automated arbitrage trading in retail FX markets using MetaTrader. Generated over 1500% ROI in 8 months with consistent performance and minimal drawdown.

	•	Infrastructure Analysis: Assessed available rack space, redundant power capacity, ambient cooling systems, and internet throughput to determine compatibility with ASIC mining hardware.
	•	Hardware Implementation: Spearheaded procurement and installation of high-performance Bitmain Antminer S19 Pros and S21s, configuring over 50 TH/s of collective hash power within three weeks.
	•	Power Efficiency Optimization: Designed PDU layout and rack configuration to optimize airflow and load distribution while minimizing electrical hotspots and bottlenecks.
	•	Mining Pool Integration: Connected the operation to a low-latency mining pool (Slushpool) for stable payouts and performance monitoring, setting up APIs for real-time dashboard visibility.
	•	Security & Remote Access: Hardened the system with firewall rules, SSH key-based access, and VPN tunneling. Enabled real-time monitoring and remote reboot capability through IPMI and custom scripts.
	•	Financial Modeling: Built a dynamic ROI calculator that accounted for Bitcoin price fluctuations, miner efficiency, and energy pricing to inform reinvestment and scale-up decisions.

Results:
	•	Operation achieved 99.98% uptime leveraging data center-grade redundancy.
	•	Net yield of ~0.1 BTC/month at peak performance.
	•	ROI achieved in 7 months with expansion into a second server bay underway.
	•	Client now operates a side business reselling hosted mining slots to other crypto investors.

headline: Global Lead Partner / Financial Executive / International Capital Markets
about:
I’m a strategic finance and operations executive with over three decades of global leadership experience helping organizations unlock value, manage risk, and scale effectively. Over my career at KPMG, I’ve guided Fortune 500 companies and multinational clients through complex transformations, regulatory shifts, and performance turnarounds, building a reputation for integrity, clarity, and execution.
As a Global Lead Partner, I lead the delivery of integrated audits across 75+ countries, orchestrating cross-functional teams and embedding technology to enhance controls, increase transparency, and elevate audit quality. Beyond audit, I drive innovation initiatives and enterprise-wide change management programs that deliver measurable operational improvements and sustained stakeholder confidence.

Previously, as Audit Practice Leader for the Pacific Southwest region, I oversaw operations across major markets, including Los Angeles, Orange County, San Diego and Phoenix. I was responsible for business unit strategy, P&L management, talent development, and client delivery, achieving a double digit CAGR over five years while navigating regulatory complexity and legacy challenges. I’ve led turnaround efforts, modernized internal processes, and built frameworks for sustainable growth across diverse business environments.

My leadership philosophy is rooted in the belief that clarity creates confidence. Whether driving cross-border operations, aligning capital strategy with growth, or advising boards and C-suite leaders, I bring a holistic approach that balances risk and opportunity, aligns people and processes, and helps organizations scale with purpose.

I’ve held leadership roles across the U.S., Europe, and Asia, including Hong Kong, where I advised companies on IPO readiness and U.S. market entry, and Germany, where I led operating initiatives and developed local U.S. GAAP/GAAS capability. I’ve also helped shape firmwide quality and governance standards as a Professional Practice Partner in New York.

With deep expertise in enterprise risk, audit quality, operational strategy, and regulatory engagement, I serve as a trusted advisor to executive teams, audit committees, and boards. I speak frequently on corporate governance, capital markets, and transformation leadership, and have served on the Advisory Board of the National Association of Corporate Directors.

A licensed CPA in Illinois and New York, I’m also an active member of the AICPA, the Illinois CPA Society, and the Executives’ Club of Chicago.

experience.position: Mergers and Acquisitions Tax Partner - National Private Equity Tax Leader
experience.description:
Richard A. Sherman is a partner in the firm’s Mergers and Acquisitions tax practice. With more than 20 years of tax consulting experience, Mr. Sherman has specialized in advising private equity and corporate clients on numerous tax aspects of mergers and acquisitions including reorganizations, acquisition and disposition planning, cross border investments, repatriations, tax modeling, restructuring and bankruptcy tax planning. Mr. Sherman’s clients cover a broad range of industries that include manufacturing, distribution, construction, transportation, business services, transaction processing, marketing services, telecommunications, industrial products, and financial services. 

Mr. Sherman also has extensive experience advising private equity clients on domestic and cross-border transactions involving tax due diligence, tax structuring and tax/financial modeling. He has also advised clients on multi-national investments including a wide variety of tax aspects including tax efficient financing structures, foreign tax credit planning, local country tax planning, and transfer pricing. In addition, Mr. Sherman has extensive experience with consolidated group tax issues, including Section 382 analyses, earnings and profits, and stock basis studies. 

Prior to joining KPMG, Mr. Sherman was a Managing Director in the Transaction Advisory Group at Alvarez and Marsal, LLC ("A&M"). At A&M, Mr. Sherman served as a Transaction Tax specialist for private equity firms and strategic corporate clients, and as an instructor for various M&A tax topics. 

Mr. Sherman holds a bachelor’s degree in Accounting from the University of Illinois, a Masters in Taxation from DePaul University, and a Juris Doctorate from Loyola University School of Law. He is a licensed Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and a CFA level II candidate in Illinois. Mr. Sherman is also a member of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, and the Illinois CPA Society.

Co-led initiative to develop and expand the private equity tax practice in Chicago and nationwide. Established client relationships with private equity firms, law firms and other corporate entities in connection with business development.
•Managed numerous tax due diligence/acquisition structuring engagements including domestic stock/asset purchases, U.S. cross border acquisitions involving PE fund AIV structuring, bankruptcy 363 sales/debt reorganizations, and leveraged refinancing transactions on behalf of middle market private equity funds ($500 million - $2 billion in capital) for acquisition targets ranging from $100 million - $1 billion in enterprise value located throughout the United States.
•Developed firm-wide technical materials and client deliverables regarding the analysis of transaction costs and their treatment for U.S. federal income tax purposes. 
•Provided tax consulting services for large corporate bankruptcies involving extensive technical research and quantitative modeling involving the partial sale and liquidation of distressed entities
•Prepared technical studies on the application of section 382 with respect to various acquisitions, the limitation of tax attributes, and strategies to enhance the utilization of such attributes 
•Structured corporate acquisitions and investments in flow-through entities, including partnerships, LLCs and S corporations, including partnership allocations and distributions.
•Reviewed quarterly and annual tax provision calculations under ASC 740 and FIN 48.

Performed tax due diligence on companies ranging in value from $100 million to $50 billion in value for medium and large private equity firms and corporations located throughout the United States involving a variety of industries, including financial services, real estate, consumer products, technology, manufacturing, retail, business services, health care, and the specialty chemical industry

• Prepared various tax models designed to highlight the foreign tax credit limitation and resulting implications on after tax cash flow from the repatriation of foreign earnings. Participated in the implementation of various acquisition financing structures, foreign debt placement and IP migration

• Participated in the development, tax modeling and implementation of various acquisition and disposition structures with respect U.S. stand alone, multinational and foreign targets

• Drafted third party opinions and tax memorandums for clients regarding tax-free reorganizations, internal restructurings, bankruptcy reorganizations 

• Prepared detailed analyses with respect to the application of section 382 on the limitation of tax attributes, and strategies to enhance the utilization of such attributes

• Prepared numerous stock basis, tax basis, and earnings and profits studies for medium and large corporate groups

• Prepared numerous current and deferred tax provisions for mid to large sized corporations under ASC 740 and FIN 48

• Performed various federal tax consulting projects involving the R&D tax credit, inventory method changes, and transaction cost studies for large corporations

slides.title: I’m a certified life coach! What now?
slides.subtitle: Malay Sapra on LinkedIn
slides.description: Becoming certified as a life coach feels like a small step in a much larger journey. While my professional journey thus far has consisted of helping large organizations grow their digital and eCommerce programs, within all my work I found a strong desire to focus on the people. Growing up and through my formal education I had always been passionate about self-improvement, growing as a person, and just being better. Reading countless books and taking tests, I always wanted to learn more about myself, human psychology, and why we are the way we are. I found myself hosting leadership retreats and attending many seminars, making connections with those who chose to be vulnerable and felt similarly. I felt a strong calling several years back as the pandemic ensued, propelling me to help others even further as I looked deep within to find meaning in my work and the impact I was making on people. While I enjoy providing consulting services, seeing people change for the better gave me the greatest joy and stronger sense of purpose in the work I do. As I explored how to do that more within my life, I instantly felt a need to pursue becoming a full-time coach and pour my heart and energy into it. Through the coursework and practice coaching sessions, I realized learning how to become a life coach was very important to me. I wanted to learn what it meant to be a life coach and to make it a part of who I am. What I didn't know was learning life coaching skills would be a part of a larger transformation that would continue to help me with my professional career, personal relationships, friendships, and everyday interactions. It was then I acknowledged that I didn't need to go into full-time coach mode. There are many definitions used for coaching and over the last year I’ve crafted my own understanding. I see it as bringing out the best from within a client by using targeted communication techniques to help them achieve their goals. This is done by accessing personal strengths and asking effective questions to drive toward an outcome. The client being coached is the expert and is responsible for the results and commitments. Through this definition and my coaching process, I also realized i'm also not the coach for everyone. I tend to gravitate towards those who are ambitious, building something and committed to being better by being self-sufficient and responsible. While I was ready to turn this new skill set into action, I realized that it wasn’t the right time for me to go into full life coach mode. Simply put, the skills I gained were what I would call “life communication skills”. By learning to put me and my needs aside in service of someone else’s desire to achieve their goals and push beyond what they had today feels empowering. I feel confident enough to facilitate conversations and as a life coach, bring out what already exists within individuals: the desire to achieve, have a meaningful purpose and live life intentionally. The techniques of holding a safe space, facilitating dialogue, and asking deep meaningful questions have inspired me to move past surface-level conversations with people in my life to seek deeper meaning with all. Today, It feels important to find deeper meaning and connection with all who exist in my life. Now, I choose to make those interactions worthwhile with every day that passes. So what’s next? While I still hold a great job, I continue to refine my new coaching skills by engaging in a coaching leadership style to lead change with all my clients and colleagues. I don’t need to practice life coaching through a formal coach and client capacity because I have the wonderful opportunity to practice it through my daily interactions. I welcome anyone who may want to work with me in a formal coaching capacity to experience the power of having someone objectively hold the space for you to make progress on goals. Until then, I look forward to continuing my journey with my new skills.

headline: Director Audit & Assurance @ KPMG | Board President @ Safe Nest
topSkills: Auditing • Management • Project Management • Communication • Accounting
about: With nearly 20 years of experience in audit and finance, I am currently a Director in Audit and Assurance Services for KPMG.  As a Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), I have successfully built and led audit teams that perform strategic and innovative risk-based audits for organizations with complex and diverse portfolios. I am passionate about adding value to operations and enhancing risk management strategies, and I enjoy working with extraordinary leaders and collaborating with cross-functional teams to achieve organizational goals.In addition to professional life, I serve as the President of the Board of Directors at Safe Nest, a comprehensive agency working to end the epidemic of domestic violence and sexual assault.  Safe Nest's mission is important to me because domestic violence is a community issue that does not discriminate. Even if you don’t know you have a personal connection, more likely than not there is someone in your life who knows hidden violence regardless of whether they have shared it with you.  If nothing else, my hope is that more of us realize a connection and choose to make a difference. Beyond work and service, I am mostly shaped by my family, friends, cats, travel, books, country music, beach life, and a lot of coffee.

experience.description: In my role at KPMG US in Las Vegas, I leverage my combination of industry and consulting experience to lead projects for clients across multiple sectors.  Returning to KPMG and specializing in internal audit and controls, I can help clients from a new and balanced perspective.  I have experience building an internal audit department from the ground up and have led financial, compliance, and operational internal audit projects in various industries including Hospitality & Gaming, Food & Beverage, Real Estate, Entertainment, Manufacturing, Distribution, and Retail & Consumer Markets.

Dreamscape’s talented team of real estate professionals has collectively deployed in excess of $35 billion in capital across residential, retail, hospitality, entertainment and gaming experiences. This team has worked on a diverse portfolio of significant properties - now including The Rio All-Suite Hotel in Las Vegas.  Beginning a $350 million renovation of the Rio in August 2023, the vision in Vegas is to honor the iconic history of the property.  

As the Director of Internal Audit I was responsible for all internal audit functions, reporting directly to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors.  It was an exciting time to be at Dreamscape and the Rio Las Vegas, working with extraordinary leaders, building the team, and transforming this property.

Caesars Entertainment, Inc. and Eldorado Resorts, Inc. came together in 2020 to create the largest gaming company in the U.S.  With over 55 properties, Caesars audit became increasingly critical. An opportunity with the Internal Audit group and a return to my professional passion, I joined Caesars as part of a specialty within the group - financial and operational audit and innovation.  In this role, I helped build our specialty audit team performing strategic and innovative risk-based audits.

Stepping away from professional life and taking on this new role, I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to devote time and focus to one of the most important jobs I’ll know.  In the meantime, I remained active as a director on two non-profit boards, as co-treasurer for our school's Parent Leadership Team, and as a finance consultant for a local animal shelter.  But for this time, if even for a short while, I mainly focused on raising a kind, loving, tiny human.

experience.position: Director of Finance, F&B and Nightclub Operations
experience.description: The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas features a combination of hotel-managed bars and restaurants, in addition to third-party managed operations, making for a diverse food and beverage (F&B) atmosphere. The knowledge and experience I gathered throughout my audit projects resulted in an opportunity to become the Director of Finance for F&B Operations.  In this role, I joined the accounting team as the controller and finance liaison for F&B general managers, both internal and third-party contacts, as well as retail partners. My responsibilities included the timely and accurate preparation of all F&B and retail reports and financial statements in compliance with US GAAP standards, including all managed and third-party outlets as well as the Marquee Nightclub & Dayclub. I also established and maintained relationships with operators and third-party finance partners, serving as the direct company contact. Additionally, I assisted with annual budgets and developed deep working relationships with management to understand operations and identify and assess process improvements.

An opportunity to join The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas as the Internal Audit Manager presented leadership experiences in gaming and hospitality that I could not refuse.  Although it was bittersweet moving away from Portland and Nike, Las Vegas quickly became home.  There, I managed financial, operational, fraud, and compliance/regulatory audits in accordance with Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX), Gaming Control Board Minimum Internal Control Standards (MICS), Payment Card Industry (PCI) Standards, and Anti Money Laundering (AML).  I will never forget my first time standing in a count room, and I would be amiss to not mention it didn’t look anything like what I learned from Ocean’s Eleven.  After a taste of the gaming audits, I focused primarily on operations including reviews of inventory management, hotel operations, security, gift card management, artwork tracking, nightclub management, and food and beverage operations.  A resort is like a little city with a variety of moving parts and, with an operational audit background, the work is limitless.

Nike is a dream company for many.  For a little girl growing up in Portland, running around the impressive headquarters as a high schooler, and already loving the brand, audit at Nike was my dream job.  I hadn’t even unpacked all my boxes from my move to Seattle when the opportunity prompted my move back to Portland to join the Nike family.

Due to the size of the company and an organizational structure called “the matrix,” Nike Corporate Audit was characterized by a considerable amount of ambiguity.  I loved it.  There, I planned and led operational and financial audits for Nike Inc. and affiliates' domestic and international operations. My various projects included approximately quarterly travel for 3 weeks at a time to Europe, Asia, and Central America.  Our team partnered with management to develop creative and innovative business-oriented solutions to improve operations, mitigate risk, ensure process effectiveness and efficiency, and meet corporate strategic objectives.  My audits included country audits of Nike Croatia, Nike Mexico, Nike China, Converse China, Nike Korea, as well as operational audits for Treasury, Corporate Talent Management (HR), and the Manufacturing Index (3rd Party Factory Scorecards).

When Evraz announced that their North American Headquarters would be moving from Portland to Chicago, a trip to the Windy City in February convinced me that I wasn’t ready for those Midwest winters. However, an opportunity at Univar ensured that I was ready for a move to the Emerald City.  At Univar, I primarily performed controls audits for our Canadian and European operations. Traveling to Canada, Belgium, and Germany, our team worked to identify control weaknesses and process improvement observations and developed recommendations to mitigate associated risks or identified inefficiencies in various areas of operations.

While exploring opportunities outside of public accounting, I considered “anything but internal audit.”  Up until this point, my experience with Internal Auditors had led me to believe that the only work I’d ever do would be testing Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) controls.  (I also imagined this to be some kind of sentence to a life behind a computer.)  To my surprise at that time, I quickly learned that internal audit is NOT that.  At Evraz, I performed operational and controls audits throughout the US and Canada.  From the melt shop, where electrodes liquefied steel for molding, to the mills rolling plate, pipe, and rail, my auditing tools sometimes included a hard hat and steel metatarsal boots.  At Evraz, I realized that I loved internal audit.

During my senior year at the University of San Diego, I realized that if I “had” to do Accounting (it was my degree after all), I’d be an auditor.  So after graduation, I moved back to Portland to start in Assurance Audit at KPMG.  As part of one of the largest firms in the city, my clients resided in a variety of industries from healthcare to electronics.  Varying industries offered unique experiences – for example, I remember being completely amazed while at a hospital reviewing paperwork for human organs.  To this day, I am grateful for the invaluable experience, exponential learning curve, and life-long friends, that came from my time at KPMG.

experience.position: Managing Director - Deal Advisory and Strategy: People Strategy COE
experience.description:
Jay has over 20 years in the human resources consulting field and specializes in coordinating the HR aspects of mergers, acquisitions and spin-offs.  He performs both buy and sell-side financial HR due diligence for a full array of private equity and strategic clients. Key areas of expertise include Defined Benefit (“DB”) Pension and Postretirement Medical (“OPEB”) Plans, Executive Agreements & Severance Plans, Internal Revenue Code Section 280G (“Golden Parachute”) issues, equity compensation analysis, and union/work councils review.

Prior to joining KPMG, he worked at PwC for 12 years in the HR Transaction group, at the Archelon Group as a trader on the Chicago Board of Options Exchange (“CBOE”), and also spent 1 year as an AmeriCorps volunteer teaching at an inter-city high school in Chicago.

Jay has a Bachelors degree in Economics and Mathematics from the University of Michigan. He is an Associate of the Society of Actuaries (ASA), an Enrolled Actuary (EA) under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) of 1974, and a Member of the American Academy of Actuaries (MAAA).

City Year was founded in 1988 on the belief that young people can change the world. City Year is an education focused, nonprofit organization that unites young people of all backgrounds for a year of full-time service to keep students in school and on track to graduation.  At City Year’s 21 urban locations across the United States and two international affiliates, teams of trained young people called corps members serve full-time in schools for the academic year as tutors, mentors and role models.  By focusing on attendance, behavior and course performance, which identify students who are at risk of dropping out, corps members are uniquely able to help students and schools succeed.

headline: National Managing Principal of Clients & Markets at KPMG LLP
topSkills: Leadership • Strategy • Client Engagement • Brand Elevation
about:
I am the National Managing Principal of Clients & Markets at KPMG U.S. In this role, I head the firm’s efforts to drive growth through strategic client engagement, market development and brand elevation while supporting the professional development and success of our people and communities. I focus on aligning KPMG’s marketing, sales and client engagement strategies with industry-specific needs across Audit, Tax and Advisory. I oversee initiatives that drive account growth, deepen sector alignment and enhance the firm’s ability to deliver tailor, high-impact solutions to clients.  

Previously, I served as the Head of Ecosystems in Advisory, where I oversaw the coordination of corporate joint ventures, technology alliances, suppliers, downstream partners, start-ups, academia, and capital investors to create value and growth opportunities for our clients. 

Prior to that, I served as U.S. Technology Consulting Leader, where I led KPMG’s Technology Enabled Transformation practice, specializing in enterprise transformation, process excellence and automation. I oversaw strategy and implementation for automation technologies, including cloud, data and AI solutions, across Fortune 100 companies and government agencies, while also developing global transformation methods and serving as a recognized thought leader and speaker in the field. 

I am committed to advancing equity and inclusion in the technology sector and broader community. I serve as an advisor to Break Through Tech, an organization dedicated to preparing students for careers in technology through academic and experiential learning. In addition, I am a board member of the Chicago Urban League, which works to empower Black families and communities through social and economic advancement.

publications.title: Business Transformation: Driving the Optimum Value
publications.description:
The right approach for transformation starts with a clear understanding of how the transformation is supporting the strategic vision and business outcomes. However, KPMG’s research reveals that many companies embark on business transformation only to be disappointed with the actual business results and value that the effort and investment achieves. This paper explores how businesses can increase their chances of success through attention to three mutually reinforcing transformation factors.

Explore these three factors in depth and learn how executives and thought leaders drive the optimum value from transformative initiatives in their organizations.

publications.title: Business Transformation and the Regulatory Environment
publications.description:
The current dynamic regulatory environment is a very important trigger of transformation. Depending on the industry sector, the regulatory environment can be a partial or dominant trigger for transformation. Regulatory compliance, though a necessity spearheaded by external factors, is an opportunity to transform and catapult a company to a new level of competitive advantage. In this paper, we outline three different approaches that companies currently employ, depending on the industry, the regulations and/or the companies’ approaches to incorporating them.

New regulations often demand complex changes, but also create a big opportunity to spearhead changes in other areas of business for those companies that are able to gain a proactive view of the current and upcoming regulatory landscape. Regulatory vigilance—including regulatory elements as part of business transformation—leads to increased acuity about transformation processes. Research shows that companies that integrate regulatory issues in the transformation framework are more likely to assess their operating models against business strategy and follow better practices regarding the processes and structuring of their transformations.

publications.title: From Burden to Competitive Advantage: Regulatory Change and Transformation in Financial Services
publications.description:
For companies in the financial services sector, the challenges of the current global regulatory environment are twofold: Regulations are expensive to implement, and they can limit revenue growth and profitability. Thus, to gain competitive advantage through a transformation, financial services firms need to design strategy and an operating model based on a regulatory framework.

Linking how you’re addressing regulatory issues along with the business strategy is incredibly important. That is a differentiator for the financial services firms that get transformation right. In this paper, we address three important steps that need to be taken to achieve a successful regulatory transformation.

about:
I completed a four year science degree in University College Dublin, specialising in Pharmacology. I then pursued the Postgraduate Diploma in Accounting in Trinity College Dublin. I spent over 3 years working in KPMG's CHEC Audit Department. CHEC covers the construction, healthcare, energy and communications sectors. I gained strong exposure to a number of big pharma, property, agriculture and biotechnology companies, working with both IFRS and US GAAP accounting standards. Thereafter I joined KPMG’s Corporate Finance team as a member of the healthcare / life science M&A team, where I also worked on life science valuation engagements. Since then, I have made the move to New York and joined the healthcare and life sciences deal advisory team, which has exposed me to financial due diligence engagements in the sector. 

I have a keen interest in the business world and the Pharmaceutical industry, particularly in areas such as Venture Capital/Private Equity, biotechnology and the drug discovery, development and commercialisation process. During my final year in university, I undertook a research project and thesis, investigating the association between the dietary consumption of seaweed and low rate of prostate cancer. As a result of this work, I gained strong experience in the laboratory, as well as an appreciation of the overall research process. 

I have continuously sought to develop my understanding of and experience in the business side of the healthcare industry: for example, through the Cancer Biology & Therapeutics Lab in UCD's relationship with OncoMark Ltd., my time as a healthcare equity analyst with Trinity's Student Managed Fund and my experience in venture capital with Fountain Healthcare Partners. Ultimately, my long term career ambition is to assume a leadership role in the Life Sciences sector.

As a UCD Student Ambassador my role was to represent and promote UCD at both on and off campus events. I participated in social, cultural and marketing and fundraising activities sponsored by the University. This opportunity allowed me to continue to develop my leadership, teamwork and communication skills. My main duties included:

To complete my undergraduate degree in Pharmacology I undertook a six month long research project and authored an accompanying thesis. I was supervised by Dr. Antoinette Perry. I worked in UCD’s Cancer Biology and Therapeutics Lab, led by Professor William Gallagher (Co-Founder and Chief Scientific Officer of OncoMark Limited – which develops novel biomarker panels to inform treatment decisions for cancer patients). My project was entitled ‘An investigation into the Chemopreventive effects of Seaweed’ and I received an A grade for my work. Specifically, it looked at whether Phlorotannin extracted from seaweed may have chemopreventive effects on prostate cancer. Chemoprevention is a relatively novel strategy to prevent cancer and involves using natural dietary compounds or synthetic substances to block, inhibit, reverse or slow carcinogenesis. Prostate cancer risk is associated with environmental factors and lifestyle including diet can play a major role in determining one’s risk of developing the disease. Long term chemopreventive strategies may decrease the rate of incidence of the cancer, one example being by increasing the intake of chemopreventive foods. The rationale for my work was that Phlorotannin is found in seaweed, which is abundantly consumed in the Asian diet. Simultaneously, the Asian population has a low rate of prostate cancer incidence, which may be partly attributable to chemopreventive substances in their diet. I gained strong analytical, time management and report writing skills from this work, and gained strong lab experience using a variety of techniques such as cell culturing, gene expression and cell viability assays, PCR, and ELISA. I was entrusted with great independence during the project and was allowed and encouraged to come up with my own experiments and form my own hypotheses , which was a tremendous learning experience and has developed transferable skills to work in business such as problem solving and data analytical skills.

In addition to the time spent in my previous position at EY for the summer, I used my own initiative to secure an extension to my contract to allow me to work in the R&D (Research and Development) Tax Department . The team has a diverse make up - with people from a technical background (science, IT, engineering etc.) working alongside those from a financial background. Together they assist a range of clients such as those in the pharmaceutical, agricultural, IT and financial services areas to make their claim. Specific tasks/experiences included:

projects.title: Bioinformatics
projects.description:
One of the biggest projects that I carried out so far was for a Bioinformatics’ module in 3rd year of university. Bioinformatics is an interdisciplinary field of science, which is a combination of computer science, statistics, mathematics and engineering, that analyses and interprets biological data. The project lasted 12 weeks, and I successfully broke the project down into a series of more manageable tasks, which I kept track of in a diary. 
The objective was to analyse a possible link between a particular protein and cancer. I carried out a large number of analyses on the protein, its receptor, its relationship with other proteins, its evolutionary history, its genome location and compounds/drugs that target the protein’s receptor. I summed up all my findings in a large report. It was a huge undertaking that involved the use of complex software, statistical tests, and making sense of large amounts of data. Overall, my protein did not have a link to leukaemia (as set out in a fictional scenario) but did have links to thyroid cancer. Furthermore, I outlined a proposed new direction of research with regards to finding the causative protein for leukaemia, while also describing future tests to continue researching my assigned protein’s link to thyroid cancer. Carrying out this project developed my analytical skills, and tested and further developed my ability to summarise all the research into a concise and clear conclusion. The report was almost 5,000 words long, and I obtained an A+ for my work.

headline: Principal at KPMG Corporate Finance LLC
about: Ted is a Principal in KPMG’s Infrastructure and Government strategy practice located in the Chicago office having primary responsibility for managing and driving client service and business development in the Midwest. Ted has significant experience in government strategy consulting as well as the use of innovative infrastructure finance and the use of public-private partnerships (PPP), including assisting public sponsors with establishing public policy objectives to effectively implement these approaches. Ted also leads KPMG’s future mobility campaign, with a focus on the impacts of connected, autonomous and electric vehicles and Mobility-as-a-Service on public and private entities.

experience.description: Ted is a senior team member of KPMG's Infrastructure Advisory practice with primary responsibility for client service and business development in the Midwest.

projects.title: Tennessee Department of Transportation Choice Lanes
projects.description: KPMG has the privilege of working with TDOT on its groundbreaking Choice Lanes program. Ted is leading the team in providing commercial, strategic, and financial advisor services to the Department.

projects.title: EV Strategy and Funding Support
projects.description: Ted is leading a broad KPMG team assisting a global energy company deploy EV charging infrastructure in the United States, leveraging Federal funding and incentives made available through the Infrastructure and Investment Jobs Act and Inflation Reduction Act.

projects.title: University of Nebraska Medical Center
projects.description: KPMG is delighted to be working with UNMC to help them and Nebraska Medicine deliver the Saddle Creek development projects. These projects include the new greenfield development of a 350,000 gsf Adminstration tower and the redevelopment of a historic facility into a healthcare incubator through innovative lease development agreements with competitively procured partners. I personally am excited as this is where I was born many years ago.

projects.title: Philadelphia 30th Street Station
projects.description: KPMG is assisting Amtrak with the redevelopment of the iconic 30th Street Station in Philadelphia through a competitive selection of a public private partner. Ted has led the team to help Amtrak develop the appropriate business and commercial structure and approach the market to bring investment and innovation to improve the overall customer experience of 30th Station users.

projects.title: OEM Hydrogen Fuel Cell Deployment
projects.description: Ted worked with a large international automotive OEM on the introduction of hydrogen fuel cell commercial vehicles. This specifically includes the development of the supply chain and infrastructure for the provisioning of green hydrogen, which is critical to advancing the adoption of such vehicles.

projects.title: AV Operator for Merced County, CA
projects.description: KPMG has worked closely with the County of Merced, CA to develop the commercial structure and help manage the procurement for a testing ground operator at the former Castle Air Force Base. This is a terrific effort and we have moved quickly to help County leadership assess the global market for OEM interest and proving ground operators and then run a competitive procurement for a 10-year operating lease at the site.

projects.title: Central Ohio Transit Authority
projects.description: KPMG has had the honor of helping COTA develop its 5-year strategic plan. We are now helping this forward looking agency develop a detailed implementation plan to achieve the goals outlined in the strategic plan.

projects.title: Dallas Area Rapid Transit
projects.description: Ted is leading a cross functional team that is working with DART leadership on the feasibility of scaling their MaaS platform. This includes a market, operating and technical feasibility analysis of the current mobile application and helping align the agency to agile deployment efforts.

projects.title: DriveOhio
projects.description: KPMG was honored to help the State of Ohio and the Ohio Department of Transportation establish DriveOhio. DriveOhio is the center for connected and autonomous vehicles across the state. We led the development of DriveOhio’s first strategic plan and collaborated closely with public and private entities to coalesce on the initiatives that support the strategic pillars of safety, mobility and workforce enhancement.

projects.title: Jacksonville Transportation Authority Autonomous Vehicle Risk Analysis
projects.description: KPMG is assisting JTA as it explores the use of autonomous vehicles for the Ultimate Urban Corridor project. We are helping conduct a risk analysis focused on the implementation and deployment of AV fleet buses.

projects.description: Led the initial structuring, project feasibility and financial analysis for the I-77 High Occupancy Toll lanes projects in Charlotte, North Carolina for the North Carolina Department of Transportation. Continued to advise NCDOT throughout the initial tendering of the project, including helping shortlist four qualified bid teams and the development of the project agreement. I-77 is a revenue risk managed lanes project and the preferred bidder was a Cintra led team that reached financial close in late 2015.

projects.title: Indiana Toll Road Restructuring
projects.description: Assisted the Indiana Finance Authority during the restructuring, bankruptcy, and retendering of the Indiana Toll Road. Ultimately the ITR was retendered resulting in IFM winning the rights to the remaining 66-years on the contract at a cost of approximately $5.8 billion. This represents an EBITDA multiple in the 30-35x range and demonstrates the strong interest pension funds have in U.S. dollar denominated assets with a history of strong consistent performance.

publications.title: Don’t Assume Your CEO Shares Your Innovation Vision
publications.description: The key to successful innovation is alignment between senior leaders and innovation teams. Yet earlier research by KPMG shows a clear disconnect between what most CEOs expect from innovation and how the company’s innovation strategy is executed.

publications.title: Make the right bets on emerging technologies
publications.description: Explore five tips for making the right bets on emerging technologies today to establish a strong foundation for a lasting culture of innovation.

publications.title: Democratizing Data: How Organizations Can Eliminate the Silos That Hinder Growth
publications.description: It is no revelation to say that the pandemic has disrupted most organizations. From sales and supply chains to finance and tax, even the best-managed organizations have scrambled to become more agile and collaborative. Despite some temporary fixes, it’s clear that taking decisive action in a constantly changing environment is hindered by data that remains heavily siloed by function and department.  This publication explores ways to address this dilemma.

publications.title: The shape of AI governance to come; A guide to creating policies, governance and oversight of AI technology
publications.description: In jurisdictions worldwide, new policy initiatives and regulations concerning the governance of data and AI signal the end of self-regulation and the rise of new oversight. As the regulatory environment continues to evolve at pace, leading organizations are addressing AI ethics and governance proactively rather than waiting for requirements to be enforced upon them.  This whitepaper examines today’s regulatory themes around AI governance from across the globe and provides organizations with a series of recommendations on how to establish trust in AI.

publications.title: Six ways technology can help organizations build agility and resilience
publications.description: Many businesses across a vast range of industries and sectors have already opened in some capacity or are working feverishly to reopen operations as fully as possible amid COVID-19, while continuing to meet the health and safety needs of employees, customers, and other key stakeholders.  KPMG has identified six ways technology can build resilience for business. This paper outlines key considerations about how to reopen responsibly, whether that means bringing employees back to workplaces, students back to classrooms, customers into shops, or loyal fans to shows and sporting events. This approach can provide the transparency stakeholders need and it can accelerate ongoing digital transformation initiatives that will build stronger operations and greater resiliency in future crises.

publications.description: KPMG Convalescent Plasma Therapy Technology Framework - Applying data virtualization, automation, analytics, and progressive web app experience to facilitate an end-to-end digital experience

publications.title: Live events and sports: Real-time technology solutions are key to a safe return
publications.description: Is enough being done to keep players and fans safe as sports return? Leveraging technology to augment manual approaches to implementing #COVID-19 safety protocols offers hope.

publications.title: Controlling AI - The imperative for transparency and explainability
publications.publishedAt: Authored by KPMG's Martin Sokalski, Swami Chandrasekaran, and Sander Klous, · Jun 28, 2019
publications.description: The power and promise of artificial intelligence (AI) can only be fully unlocked when we gain greater trust, transparency, and control over the technology, algorithms, and data. This is why companies need to institute effective governance methods for AI, with a focus on responsibly unleashing the power of these technologies. The paper will share approaches and methodologies to do so.

publications.title: Customer trust in technology
publications.description: As technology fuels the digital age, IT has never been more important in influencing the customer experience and shaping customer interactions. In the near future, technology leaders will face a significant challenge—customer trust. The importance of trust is becoming more dependent on complex, often invisible, connected technologies, data streams and third parties. But people instinctively distrust things they can’t see, touch or understand.

publications.title: Enduring the IoT Storm to unlock new paths to value
publications.description: The internet of things (IoT) is poised for exponential growth in nearly every industry and marketplace. As companies seek competitive advantages through deeper insights, consumers demand technology in everyday products, and organizations continue to increase reliance on interconnected technology; this ecosystem has become increasingly complex. With the sheer number of stakeholders, each exposed to unique threats posed by connected devices—how are forward-looking companies avoiding unforeseen risk exposure, redundant costs, and other issues that can bring an IoT program to a grinding halt?

publications.title: Intelligent automation takes flight - Risk and governance will help you safely land your automation goals
publications.description:
Given the clear benefits and countless use cases, it’s no wonder intelligent automation has become a mission critical initiative. The race is on and there is simply no turning back. But as a leader in one of the many organizations considering a takeoff—or already in flight—you know embarking on such a broad and important digital transformation project is no time to throw caution to the wind.

That’s where intelligent automation risk and governance comes in. A well designed risk and governance function helps ensure your intelligent automation program avoids a turbulent flight or a crash landing—that any and all risks associated with the digital transformation are effectively identified, evaluated and mitigated (or in some cases, accepted).

about:
A results-oriented financial services professional with deep expertise in guiding global banking institutions through complex, cross-border regulatory challenges. Over the past 9 years, I have built a reputation for successfully leading and supporting multi-faceted transformation programs that address critical non-financial risks.

Core Specializations:
•	Operational & Enterprise Risk: Designing and implementing robust risk management frameworks that strengthen control environments.
•	Regulatory Compliance: Leading remediation efforts and ensuring adherence to evolving regulatory requirements and mandates.
•	Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM): Establishing rigorous governance structures for vendor and partner ecosystems.

Areas of Expertise:
• Stakeholder Management • Risk Appetite & Culture • Project Management • Internal Control Frameworks • Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) • Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) • Regulatory Examination & Remediation • Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) • Change Management • Business Transformation • Cross-Functional Collaboration • Non-Financial & Operational Risk

I excel at fostering enterprise-wide collaboration, securing buy-in from senior executives, and leading teams to not only achieve compliance but also to drive process optimization, improve data integrity, and build a resilient, risk-aware organization.

experience.description:
Support global banking and FinTech clients in enterprise-wide risk transformation and regulatory remediation, providing strategic advisory to strengthen governance, operations, and risk oversight.

Key achievements include:

• Leading engagement delivery across multiple client portfolios, which involved overseeing risk assessments, control testing, and regulatory remediation to nail those evolving global compliance standards. 

• Partnering with cross-functional teams to strengthen governance and efficiency—improving data integrity and reporting accuracy using automation and compliance solutions. 

• Developing and implementing tailored risk and compliance solutions that boost governance and control effectiveness across entire enterprise functions. 

• Advising executive leadership on regulatory trends and compliance modernization, and expertly managing stakeholder communications throughout. 

• Conducting comprehensive lifecycle assessments of regulatory changes to identify gaps, define remediation roadmaps, and validate successful implementation outcomes.

• Providing leadership and mentorship to Associates and interns, promoting high-quality delivery, teamwork, and professional growth.

• Driving business growth by enhancing go-to-market strategies and identifying opportunities to expand client relationships in risk services.

experience.position: Senior Management Consultant – Finance, Risk & Compliance
experience.description:
Advised premier financial institutions on transforming risk and compliance functions, with a focus on strengthening non-financial risk management, AML frameworks, and regulatory preparedness.

Key achievements included:

• Directing cross-functional project teams and expertly managing client relationships, ensuring the timely and high-quality delivery of complex risk transformation and compliance initiatives. 

• Orchestrating enhanced risk and control frameworks that successfully strengthened governance structures and truly embedded compliance into enterprise operations. 

• Advancing AML risk assessment methodologies and regulatory response processes, which led to significant improvements in data integrity, control effectiveness, and overall program governance. 

• Leading and mentoring consultant teams, providing coaching and professional development that elevated our delivery standards and maximized client impact. 

• Facilitating daily client working sessions to review deliverables and recommending process improvements that boosted compliance efficiency and audit readiness. 

• Partnering with business and technology leaders to operationalize regulatory requirements into clear, actionable policies, procedures, and system enhancements, directly supporting enterprise compliance objectives.

Focused on driving informed financial analysis, forecasting, and risk assessment, partnering closely with senior leadership to align liquidity management, stress testing, and capital planning with supervisory requirements.

Key achievements included:

• Developing and maintaining robust CCAR and DFAST forecasting models, which ensured strict compliance with Dodd-Frank and Federal Reserve stress testing requirements—a critical component of our regulatory posture. 

• Performing daily treasury operations, including meticulous cash flow monitoring, short-term liquidity forecasting, and detailed balance sheet variance analysis to support key funding and investment decisions. 

• Preparing and analyzing complex financial reports and key performance metrics that were essential for guiding executive decision-making on critical issues like capital allocation and risk exposure. 

• Collaborating closely with Internal Audit and Risk Management teams to evaluate treasury controls, which ultimately enhanced data integrity and strengthened adherence to regulatory standards.
